title: Mindspark helps Delhi students improve their math and Hindi scores
summary: Students offered free access to Mindspark centers gained 0.37 standard deviations in math and 0.23 in Hindi over 4.5 months.
account: Educational Initiatives ran three after-school Mindspark centers in Delhi. Sessions combined 45 minutes of adaptive exercises with 45 minutes of instruction in small groups. The software used teaching rules that specialists had written. A lottery offered 314 of 619 students a voucher that waived the fee. The final study reports that voucher recipients gained 0.37 standard deviations in math and 0.23 in Hindi between September 2015 and February 2016. Average attendance was 58%, and 539 students completed endline tests. The estimate concerns the combined program. All three centers closed in March 2016 after enrollment remained below the threshold for continued subsidy.
purpose: Mindspark was built to personalize instruction to each student's measured level. The test-score gains are that purpose.
system: Mindspark, with rules that adapt exercises to students’ answers and errors, alongside small-group instruction

ratings.reason: Students had measurable gains in math and Hindi.
